content: To apply the eye medication, first wash your hands thoroughly. Avoid wearing contact lenses while you have an eye infection or are using this medication. Tilt your head back, look upward, and gently pull down the lower eyelid to create a small pouch. Hold the dropper directly above your eye and place one drop into the pouch. After applying the drop, look downward, gently close your eyes, and use one finger to apply light pressure to the inner corner of your eye (near the nose) for 1 to 2 minutes. This technique helps prevent the medication from draining out. Avoid blinking or rubbing your eye after application. Do not rinse the dropper. If you are using another type of eye medication, such as drops or ointments, wait at least 5 minutes between applications. Use this medication consistently to achieve the best results. To help you remember, apply it at the same times each day. Continue using the medication for the full duration prescribed by your doctor, even if your symptoms improve after a few days. Temporary blurred vision and mild eye irritation or redness may occur after applying this medication. These side effects are usually not serious. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. If you experience any unusual or severe symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. Before using ganciclovir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, valganciclovir, or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. After applying the medication, your vision may become temporarily blurred, so avoid driving or operating machinery until your vision clears. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It is not known if this drug passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.) immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it for other conditions unless directed by your doctor. While using this medication, your doctor may recommend regular lab or medical tests, such as eye exams, to monitor your progress. Keep all medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature and protect it from freezing. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Consult your pharmacist or local waste disposal company for guidance on safe disposal. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
